what_to_observe: The trigger, frequency, cost and person responsible are clear
example_pass_signal: The customer can show the last real instance of the task

what_to_observe: Time, errors, missed steps, duplicate entry and current tools are documented
example_pass_signal: A before-state exists for the same task and time window

what_to_observe: The customer can explain what should improve and why it matters
example_pass_signal: The expected business result is specific and observable

what_to_observe: Shared devices, power, data cost, connection quality and user access are checked
example_pass_signal: The actual operator can complete the task on the device they use

what_to_observe: Inputs, owners, approvals, missing information and failure paths are visible
example_pass_signal: No required step depends on an undocumented workaround

what_to_observe: Only the fields, roles and notifications needed for the chosen job are enabled
example_pass_signal: A new user can see the next action without a feature tour

what_to_observe: The product handles a real customer or business record
example_pass_signal: The customer confirms the result is correct and useful

check: Complete the task again without live help
what_to_observe: The same user repeats the job without a trainer guiding each action
example_pass_signal: The task is completed independently on a later working day

what_to_observe: Another team member can continue the workflow and understand its state
example_pass_signal: A second person completes their part without chasing the first user

what_to_observe: The team knows which record is authoritative and when the old record is only a fallback
example_pass_signal: No routine double-entry is needed for the chosen task

what_to_observe: Missing input, changed order, lost connection or an incorrect record is handled visibly
example_pass_signal: The user can identify what is saved, pending and who must act

what_to_observe: Calls, messages and manual corrections needed per completed task
example_pass_signal: Support needs decline as the customer repeats the task

what_to_observe: Task coverage, time, rework, handoff and customer confidence are compared
example_pass_signal: The customer sees a useful improvement against the agreed baseline
Evidence is reviewed with the customer-side owner
owner: The next step is recorded with a reason and an owner
